title: Out of Time to Delay, House to Vote on Trump’s Power to Continue War in Iran
partialText: A measure to direct the president to halt U.S. engagement in Iran had been on track to pass in late May, but Republican leaders postponed action. They have run out of time to delay the vote.

title: Six Questions Out of Tuesday’s Big Primaries in California, Iowa and Elsewhere
partialText: Who will run California? Can Democrats win Iowa? Here’s what happened, and what might be next.

title: Trump Administration Fights Court Order to Refund Some Tariffs
partialText: The administration has started to repay some of the money, but has signaled it may make it harder for certain businesses to claim the full amount they are owed.

title: Trump Administration Turns to a New Rationale to Justify Old Tariffs
partialText: The administration has settled on a more legally and politically durable way to impose tariffs, but some say the focus on forced labor is merely a pretext for protectionism.

title: New Intelligence Role Puts Bill Pulte’s Housing Agenda in Doubt
partialText: Mr. Pulte has had difficulty boosting the housing market as head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency. Now he will also serve as acting intelligence director.

title: ‘Infuriated’ Former Judges Take on Trump
partialText: Critics say it is unseemly for retired judges to trade on the prestige of their former positions.

title: How Taylor Swift Writes a Song, In Her Own Words
partialText: The artist shares stories behind some of her biggest hits, her love of a “rant bridge” and how life in the public eye informs the stories she tells in her songs.

title: Bari Weiss Speaks on Scott Pelley’s ’60 Minutes’ Firing: ‘That’s the Path That He Chose’
partialText: In her first public comments on the firing, Ms. Weiss, the CBS News editor in chief, said that the longtime correspondent had “broken” the trust in the newsroom.

title: See the Clashes Between ICE and Protesters in New Jersey
partialText: Demonstrations outside the Delaney Hall immigrant detention center have at times turned violent, with the authorities deploying tear gas and wielding batons as protesters resisted calls to disperse.

title: A New Play, ‘Kenrex,’ Revisits the Story of a Bully’s Unsolved Murder
partialText: A man was shot dead surrounded by witnesses in Skidmore, Mo., but no one was ever prosecuted. Now that act of vigilante justice has inspired the play “Kenrex.”

title: For Knicks’ Owner James Dolan, a Title Might Finally Stop Some Boos
partialText: James Dolan, the longtime owner of the N.B.A. team, has faced years of jeers. Could a championship change all that?

title: Want Courtside Seats for the Knicks? Be Rich, Famous and a Die-Hard Fan.
partialText: Prime tickets on the floor for the N.B.A. Finals are coveted and very hard to get. The No. 1 requirement: You must love the Knicks.

title: Charleston’s Charm Hides Bloody History of Revolutionary War in South Carolina
partialText: Some of the fiercest battles took place in South Carolina, but its part in the fight for independence is often overlooked. Our reporter found history, myths, beauty and contradiction across the Lowcountry landscapes.

title: Only the Right Tests Can Stop This Ebola Outbreak. Congo Has Hardly Any.
partialText: A chronic lack of investment in development of better tests has left clinicians blind and allows deadly viruses to spread unchecked.

title: I Went to Lebanon and Found Something Strangely Hopeful
partialText: It just needs to be given the chance.

title: Feeling Nihilistic? You’re Not Alone.
partialText: A case for mourning the American dream.

title: Painted Into a Corner
partialText: We look at the state of the Iran war three months on.

title: At Interlochen, Where Jeffrey Epstein’s Shadow Still Lingers
partialText: The arts school and camp is still contending with the fallout from its former ties to Mr. Epstein, an alumnus and donor accused of preying on two girls he met there.
